opinions.name: Custom orchestration
opinions.point: scout/chef split made the biggest difference
opinions.quote: Splitting read-only research ('scouts' on a fast/cheap model) from code changes ('chefs' running in isolated git worktrees that must pass a deterministic check before merging) made the biggest difference for me.

opinions.name: Chinese open-weight models
opinions.point: wrote correct code, but saved no money
opinions.quote: Last month we tested 6 Chinese models on a real coding job. All of them wrote correct code, but since we're on flat-rate plans, none saved us money, so we didn't switch.

opinions.name: Claude Code
opinions.point: stock CLI plus skills was enough
opinions.quote: Stock Claude Code CLI, in tmux on a server… Never switched. The default plus skills got us there.

opinions.name: OpenClaw
opinions.point: nowhere near their Claude Code-based system
opinions.quote: We tried OpenClaw, Hermes Agent and Grok Bot. None of them came close to what we built on Claude Code, so we dropped them.

opinions.name: Hermes Agent
opinions.point: nowhere near their Claude Code-based system
opinions.quote: We tried OpenClaw, Hermes Agent and Grok Bot. None of them came close to what we built on Claude Code, so we dropped them.

opinions.name: Grok bot
opinions.point: nowhere near their Claude Code-based system
opinions.quote: We tried OpenClaw, Hermes Agent and Grok Bot. None of them came close to what we built on Claude Code, so we dropped them.

opinions.name: OpenCode
opinions.point: open source, switch models and providers freely
opinions.quote: OpenCode as the coding agent. Moved off Claude Code mostly because it's open source and I can switch models/providers and use subscriptions I already pay for.

opinions.name: Claude Code
opinions.point: ties the workflow to one vendor
opinions.quote: Moved off Claude Code mostly because it's open source [OpenCode]… I don't want my whole workflow tied to one vendor when models change every few months.

opinions.name: Herdr
opinions.point: shows which parallel session needs attention
opinions.quote: herdr to keep parallel sessions alive… terminal tabs fell apart fast. The useful part is seeing which session is working, which is blocked, and which needs me.

opinions.name: Claude Code
opinions.point: plain setup that works for a solo project
opinions.quote: Fairly boring setup, but it works for a solo project: - Claude Code in the project folder, nothing fancy on top.

opinions.name: Custom orchestration
opinions.point: coordinator agents narrate instead of working
opinions.quote: I've tried coordinator agents; they spend more tokens narrating progress than working, and the review burden does not go away.

opinions.name: Lyre
opinions.point: keeps app preview live while agent edits
opinions.quote: Lyre runs the agent and the preview as separate lifecycles, which is what puts device testing inside the edit loop instead of after it.

opinions.name: LangGraph
opinions.point: right control for devs, opaque to non-developers
opinions.quote: settled on LangGraph for anything serious… For a developer it's the right level of control. Where it falls down is the moment a non-developer needs to own a workflow

opinions.name: Claude Code
opinions.point: hooks wire agent into the machine deterministically
opinions.quote: Claude Code's hooks (UserPromptSubmit / PostToolUse / Stop / SessionEnd) and Cursor's hooks.json let you wire the agent into the rest of your machine deterministically, which turned out to matter more to me than the UI.

opinions.name: Cursor
opinions.point: good diff review UI and hooks
opinions.quote: Cursor when I want the diff review UI… Cursor's hooks.json let you wire the agent into the rest of your machine deterministically

opinions.name: Git worktrees
opinions.point: unglamorous but survives crashes
opinions.quote: Multiple terminal tabs and git worktrees, which is unglamorous but survives a crash better than anything clever I tried.

opinions.name: Claude
opinions.point: weekly usage limits are the biggest pain
opinions.quote: I mostly use Claude Code (the desktop app), on a Max plan… Biggest pain: weekly usage limits.

opinions.name: Claude Code
opinions.point: used most of the day, beyond coding
opinions.quote: Honestly, Claude Code is where I spend most of my day now, and not only for code.

opinions.name: Custom orchestration
opinions.point: writing code easy, self-verification was hard
opinions.quote: We did build an internal agent that takes a GitHub issue, implements it… Biggest surprise: getting it to write code was easy. Getting it to verify its own work and stop to ask when unsure took most of the effort.

opinions.name: Subagents (built-in)
opinions.point: subagents caused surprise costs
opinions.quote: The number I actually watch is cost per session, subagents included, that is where the surprises were.

opinions.name: Claude
opinions.point: couldn't go back; Opus covers everything
opinions.quote: got a free Max trial coupon and couldn't go back… No, Opus 5.5 covers basically everything.

opinions.name: Custom assistant
opinions.point: good for privacy, but Whisper hallucinations
opinions.quote: Local voice stack… Works well for privacy-sensitive use cases. But auditing it revealed a nasty failure mode: Whisper hallucinating "Amara.org" subtitle credits on near-silence

opinions.name: LangGraph
opinions.point: agents loop endlessly without custom safeguards
opinions.quote: we've been running a mix of LangGraph and CrewAI… the hardest part hasn't been getting them to work, it's been stopping them from working too much… it feels like something that should just be built into the frameworks by now.

opinions.name: CrewAI
opinions.point: agents loop endlessly without custom safeguards
opinions.quote: we've been running a mix of LangGraph and CrewAI… the hardest part hasn't been getting them to work, it's been stopping them from working too much… it feels like something that should just be built into the frameworks by now.

opinions.name: cmux
opinions.point: faster than Warp; sessions can talk
opinions.quote: I used to use Warp, but switched to cmux. It feels faster, and it lets Claude sessions running on different accounts talk to each other.

opinions.name: Anthropic API
opinions.point: Haiku cheap for loops, Opus for planning
opinions.quote: for the boring loops i just drop to haiku 5.5 ($0.10/$0.50 per 1m) and keep opus for planning. same harness, way less burn

opinions.name: Custom orchestration
opinions.point: coordinator keeps track across many sessions
opinions.quote: I never trusted the multi-agent hype, but now that I use it I have a hard time going back… After several weeks of one agent coordinating tens of sessions… it still doesn't seem to lose track of what anyone worked on.

opinions.name: Hermes Agent
opinions.point: useful continuity, but unreliable and needs maintenance
opinions.quote: Reliability is still a weak point [with Hermes]. I've had interrupted scheduled jobs, gateway hangs and unexplained host restarts… I get enough useful work out of the setup to keep using it, but it also creates maintenance work.
